section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion summarizes results from a single study of female undergraduates finding that body appreciation, media influence (SATAQ-3 subscales), and participant BMI significantly predicted consideration of cosmetic surgery, accounting for 47.1% of variance, with body appreciation the strongest predictor. The authors note BMI predicted consideration in an unexpected direction (more slender participants reported greater consideration) and that respondent age was negatively correlated with consideration but was not a significant predictor. Limitations include the restricted undergraduate sample and limited variables, and the authors recommend replication in community samples and inclusion of additional psychological variables.
